title: SR-1.34 A daemon start waits long enough for a slow machine, a kept daemon ends, and one daemon serves
request: Closes the open follow-up 'Raise the daemon start wait' (docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md, found 1 Nov 2026; not in the gap register of the investment analysis) and covers the start path of the open question 'Session start on a slow machine': startDaemon and ensureDaemon wait 6000 ms (src/cli/daemon.mjs:69 and :76) and then stop the daemon they began (daemon.mjs:93). On a slow Windows runner the daemon has not reached listen by then (src/server/main.mjs takes daemon.lock at :28 after its static imports, opens the vault at :30 and logs 'cannot listen' in the handler after that), so it is stopped before it can write its log: the start reports 'did not start', the listen-error line is never written, and a session-start hook shows 'Memev is not reachable' instead of the resume card (hooks.mjs:192). The ceiling is a provisional 30 s, a proxy from the Windows job's CI logs (12.7 s is a whole test's duration, not a daemon start time; see the task description). Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-1.01 and SR-1.24 (signed in their second versions, k-sr-1-01-one-writer-enfor-f59dc6 and k-sr-1-24-no-cli-command-w-adb5d2, and left untouched; both are signed and NOT built on main: there is no oplog lock, and with daemon.lock removed two daemons serve one vault). The build of this contract starts after SR-1.01 T1 and T3 land, because its one-writer criteria assert at the oplog lock. Claim F, not D: Claim D is the seed-readiness follow-ups in general, but this task changes the same files as the signed one-writer contracts (daemon.mjs, server/main.mjs, cli/main.mjs) and is built by the same builder right after them, so one claim holds the sequence. Sensitive path: none (the oplog is read, not changed).

tasks.title: A start waits long enough for a slow machine, a kept daemon ends, and one daemon serves
requirements: src/cli/daemon.mjs exports START_WAIT_MS, 30000 by default, a provisional ceiling and not a fact: it is 2 x 12.7 s rounded up, and 12.7 s is the longest whole-test duration of a failed start in the Windows job's CI logs, not a daemon start time (see 'The ceiling' below). It is read once from MEMEV_START_WAIT_MS as requirement 2 says (the same override pattern as MEMEV_STATE_TIMEOUT_MS in SR-1.24, with a stricter parse), and it is the default wait of ensureDaemon and startDaemon in place of 6000 (daemon.mjs:69, :76). The wait is a ceiling, not a delay: the loop returns as soon as this vault's daemon answers and stops as soon as the child exits with anything but 3. The new exports (START_WAIT_MS, HOOK_START_WAIT_MS) are imported dynamically only in tests, so a test that runs at base main fails on its assertion and not on a missing export

the env waits and the marker are validated, so the ceiling cannot be defeated: MEMEV_START_WAIT_MS, MEMEV_HOOK_START_WAIT_MS and MEMEV_START_NOTICE_MS are accepted only when the whole string is a plain decimal integer of one to nine digits (no sign, space, exponent, fraction or hex), else the default applies; an accepted value is clamped into [1000, 600000], [100, 600000] and [100, 600000] respectively, and 600000 is below 2^31 - 1, because setTimeout fires after 1 ms for a larger delay and a daemon would be killed at once; a loop that compares dates is not used to wait, so no value can keep a start 'starting' for ever. The marker is validated where it is read: spawned_at and deadline_at must be integers and deadline_at - spawned_at must be positive and at most 600000, else it is no marker (not starting, not a deadline), and the daemon falls back to MEMEV_START_WAIT_MS from its environment. An explicit waitMs option is capped at 600000 too

the hook wait stays 6 s: today hooks.mjs:84 passes no waitMs and gets the 6000 default, so the spec does not change it. src/cli/hooks.mjs exports HOOK_START_WAIT_MS = 6000, read from MEMEV_HOOK_START_WAIT_MS, and passes it on every event, so raising the default to 30 s does not reach the hooks. Whether a hook should wait less is an open owner decision (question (b) below). The stop and pre-compact hooks (hooks.mjs:62-66; the stop hook's contract gate must not fail open and the pre-compact checkpoint must land) keep today's behaviour exactly: wait HOOK_START_WAIT_MS, then stop the daemon they began

a kept start: startDaemon takes { keep = false } and ensureDaemon forwards it. A start with keep: true does not stop the daemon it began when its wait ends; the child is left to come up, and its own deadline (requirement 6) ends it if it does not. Only session-start and prompt pass keep: true, because a hook that stops its daemon at 6 s on a slow machine never gets one up. Every other caller, and the default, is not kept

a start marker: right after spawn startDaemon writes .memev/daemon.starting.json { pid, spawned_at, deadline_at, caller } (mode 0600, written with an exclusive rename so a reader never sees half of it), and removes it when the daemon is serving, when a start that is not kept stops its child, or when the daemon exits. It serves four uses: (1) 'starting' detection: a daemon is starting when the marker's pid is alive, now is before deadline_at, and /healthz does not answer; a marker past deadline_at, or whose pid is dead, is not starting, so a wedged live pid never reads as starting for ever; (2) the kept daemon's deadline; (3) start-time logging; (4) no second child while one is starting. daemon.lock is taken only after src/server/main.mjs has loaded its static imports (server/main.mjs:28, after lines 1-9 and the config check at :19-22), so a cold module load on a slow disk has no lock at all and the marker is the only sign of a start in that phase. 'The daemon is present' is read as SR-1.24 reads it (.memev/daemon.lock or daemon.json names a live pid, or the SR-1.01 vault lock is held by a pid one of them names), with the marker as one more name

a kept daemon ends: src/server/main.mjs (not src/cli/main.mjs) arms a deadline when it begins, from deadline_at in the marker, or from MEMEV_START_WAIT_MS in its environment when there is none. If it has not reached listen by then it writes '[memev] no listen by the deadline (<N> ms); exiting', removes daemon.lock and the marker, and exits non-zero (a daemon that fails earlier exits at once on that failure, as today: 3, 4, 5). The deadline is cleared when the daemon reaches listen. Nothing else reaches a hook's child: daemon.mjs:93 stops only the child of the process that is still running, and a hook has exited. memev stop stops a kept daemon (requirement 7)

stopDaemon (daemon.mjs:98-100) finds a starting daemon that has no daemon.json from the marker and daemon.lock, and stops it: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after its wait, and daemon.lock and the marker are removed only after the process is dead. It never deletes the lock of a live starting daemon and leaves the process running, as daemon.mjs:100 does today when daemon.json is missing (the lock and daemon.json are removed and the live daemon goes on holding the vault). A pid named by a marker or a lock is checked against its recorded start time when SR-1.01 T1's start-time reader exists, so a reused pid is not signalled; before that the marker's age bound is the check (an open question below)

one daemon under concurrent starters: startDaemon first reads the marker and daemon.lock; when the marker names a live starting pid (within deadline_at) or daemon.lock names a live pid, it does not spawn a child, it waits on that pid, as a start that was not kept does for its own wait, and returns true when it answers. A child that exits 3 (daemon.lock held, server/main.mjs:28) or 5 (the oplog lock held, which SR-1.01 T3 makes the daemon's exit code; today 5 also means an invalid .memev/config.json, server/main.mjs:21) waits on its holder only while the holder is alive: the holder is the pid that daemon.lock, the start marker or .memev/oplog/LOCK names; when that pid is dead the wait ends at once (today it runs to the end of the wait, daemon.mjs:88-90 and, with a 30 s ceiling, would burn 30 s) and returns false, or spawns once more when no marker is live, and an exit of 5 with no live holder (an invalid config) ends the start at once. A start that did not begin the daemon never stops it when its own wait ends. The property is asserted at the oplog lock level (SR-1.01 T1's .memev/oplog/LOCK names one pid) and at the daemon.lock level together; SR-1.01 T1 and T3 are signed and not built on main, so this task is built after them (Claim F builds them first, in order), and until T3 lands only the daemon.lock-level assertions can pass

start time is logged, a measurable line: the daemon appends '[memev] serving <root> on http://<bind>:<port> (<N> ms since spawn)', N from spawned_at in the marker, so a kept daemon whose parent has exited is measured too; the cannot-listen line carries the same count; a start that gives up appends '[memev] gave up after <N> ms waiting for pid <pid>'. The next revision of the ceiling is set from these lines

the 14 callers that the new 30 s default reaches are listed, each as intended: src/cli/main.mjs:273 (init), :307 (memev start), :310 (memev restart), :323 and :341 (commands that need the daemon), src/cli/doctor.mjs:319 (the 'start it' fix action of doctor --fix, run: () => startDaemon(...)) and :324 (its restart), src/cli/memory-cli.mjs:8, src/cli/contracts-cli.mjs:92, src/cli/import.mjs:22, src/engine/importers/core.mjs:174, src/cli/bus-cli.mjs:72 and :100, and src/cli/mcp-stdio.mjs:13. A person or a script that started the daemon is better served by a wait that outlasts a slow machine than by an error; each of these is a command the person ran, or a library call inside one, and none holds an agent turn. A start still waiting after MEMEV_START_NOTICE_MS (default 6000) prints one stderr line, 'Memev is still starting; waiting up to <ceiling> s (see <path of daemon.log>)', from each of them except mcp-stdio, which runs inside a protocol and stays silent, and the hook path, which has its own text. The alternative, keeping 6 s for the library callers, is an owner decision (below)

the session-start card says 'Memev is starting' only on the ensureDaemon-false path (hooks.mjs:84, caught at :192) and only while the start marker says starting (requirement 5): the card carries no pid, no path and no error text. The 4000 ms call timeout at hooks.mjs:86 keeps today's text, and so does every case where nothing is starting. The prompt hook's notice (hooks.mjs:198, 'Memev could not start') says 'Memev is starting' in the same case. This spec does not decide question (b), whether session-start should get a longer timeout, a retry or a different message in general

the test seams are restricted to tests and named: MEMEV_TEST_SEAMS=1 must be set for any of them to act (a stricter guard than MEMEV_LOCK_TEST_PAUSE's, below). MEMEV_START_TEST_DELAY_MS=<ms> makes startDaemon launch the daemon through a wrapper that waits that long before importing src/server/main.mjs (the cold module load, before daemon.lock exists; startDaemon, not main.mjs, reads it, because main.mjs's static imports run first). MEMEV_START_TEST_HOLD=before-listen makes src/server/main.mjs stop after it has the lock and the vault and before it calls listen (a daemon that never serves). MEMEV_START_TEST_SPAWN_LOG=<file> makes main.mjs append its pid when it begins. The guard is stricter than the one MEMEV_LOCK_TEST_PAUSE has in SR-1.01 (which is not restricted): the switch is process.env.MEMEV_TEST_SEAMS === '1' exactly (unset, '0', 'true' and '' leave every seam off), the variables are read only from process.env, only in daemon.mjs and src/server/main.mjs, and while a seam is active the daemon appends '[memev] test seam active: <variable name>' to daemon.log, so a leaked MEMEV_START_TEST_HOLD is visible and not a silent stop

Ctrl-C leaves the detached child (daemon.mjs:81, detached: true) running when the parent of a start is interrupted; the spec states it and covers it with the kept-daemon deadline: the child serves or is dead by its deadline. No handler is added for SIGINT

the one-writer and deadline criteria run on Linux. Windows is out of scope of this task: SIGTERM and SIGKILL semantics, pid liveness and file locking differ there, no Windows test is written, and the Windows CI job (which runs on pushes to main only) is where it would show. The removal of the doctor MEM-006 AC02 retry (requirement 17) is confirmed on the first Windows run after merge: test/daemon-start-wait.test.mjs is not in the Windows job, and the Windows job runs on pushes to main only. If that run shows the start flaking, the retry is put back by a separate revert. Landing the removal separately was not chosen, because it would need a Windows run as well and would leave main with the retry and the long wait together. Whether to add a Windows run of the new test is an owner decision

each red-green criterion has its own subtest whose name starts with its task position (T1-c01: for the first) and the criterion runs only that subtest; each subtest's first assertion fails at base main on an assertion, not on a TypeError or a load error (the new exports are imported dynamically; the first assertion of most tests is START_WAIT_MS === 30000, and the hook ones HOOK_START_WAIT_MS === 6000). The waits are shortened through the env overrides (MEMEV_START_WAIT_MS, MEMEV_HOOK_START_WAIT_MS, MEMEV_START_NOTICE_MS), so no test sleeps for the real 6 s or 30 s, which matters for the per-mutant reruns of QL-1.02

tasks.description:
The ceiling. 30 s is provisional. The Windows job's CI logs hold no daemon start-to-serving time: a test reports its own duration and a pass or fail, and the daemon log is not in the log. They show that the daemon had not served within the 6 s wait in every one of the 8 failures of doctor MEM-006 AC02 (the daemon is then stopped, daemon.mjs:93, so how long it needed cannot be seen). The proxy is the longest whole-test duration of a failed start that no poll lengthened, 12.7 s (run 41244882353 attempt 1, job 124666127747: vault creation, the 6 s wait and two onboarding runs); the others took 7.6, 8.3, 8.4, 8.9, 9.8 and 11.0 s, and the one with the 20 s poll took 30.6 s (run 41274568215 attempt 1, job 124754017252). 2 x 12.7 s = 25.4 s, rounded up to 30 s. The pull request lists every value. The ceiling is re-set from the 'ms since spawn' lines once they exist.

Does not decide: (a) the prompt hook's recall budget (HOOK_BUDGET_MS, 1500 ms; the open question 'Prompt hook recall over its budget'), (b) whether session-start should get a longer timeout, a retry or a different message in general (the open question 'Session start on a slow machine'; this task covers only the start path), (c) the prompt hook's score bar (the open question 'Prompt hook score threshold').

Scope overlaps: SR-1.01 T3 and SR-1.24 T1 (src/cli/daemon.mjs, src/server/main.mjs, src/cli/main.mjs, signed and not built; this task is built after them), SR-1.11 T1 (daemon.mjs and server/main.mjs: memev stop's bound), SR-1.05 T1 (server/main.mjs), SR-1.28 T1 and T2, SR-1.29 T1 and SR-1.31 T1 (hooks.mjs, cli/main.mjs), SR-1.30 T1 (hooks.mjs, mcp-stdio.mjs, test/helpers/**), SR-2.03 T1 (hooks.mjs, test/helpers/cli.mjs). Their changes to the shared files are merged in order; none names the start wait or the start marker.

Owner decisions this spec makes and lists: (1) the hook wait stays 6 s and the question whether it should be shorter is left to question (b); (2) the 30 s default reaches 14 call sites, each listed as intended, with a progress line after 6 s, instead of keeping 6 s for the library callers; (3) a hook's start is kept (not stopped at the end of its wait) for session-start and prompt only; (4) Windows is out of scope, and the removal of the doctor retry is confirmed on the first Windows run after merge; (5) a pid named by a marker or lock is signalled by stop only inside the marker's age bound until SR-1.01 T1's start-time reader exists; (6) the accepted range of the env waits (1000 to 600000 ms for the start wait, 100 to 600000 for the hook wait and the notice) and the nine-digit strict parse; (7) the test seams need MEMEV_TEST_SEAMS exactly '1', and a leaked seam is logged.
